claims.text: Elevated-temperature stress–strain behavior in HfNbTaTiZr is explained by interactions among dislocations, grain boundaries, and solute atoms.
The thermal expansion of HfNbTaTiZr is explained by interactions among dislocations, grain boundaries, and solute atoms.
The elevated-temperature elastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr is explained by interactions among dislocations, grain boundaries, and solute atoms.
The interactions among dislocations, grain boundaries, and solute atoms change with temperature and strain rate.
Dislocation slip is an operative deformation mechanism in HfNbTaTiZr at elevated temperature.
Grain-boundary sliding is an operative deformation mechanism in HfNbTaTiZr at elevated temperature.
Solute-atom diffusion is an operative deformation mechanism in HfNbTaTiZr at elevated temperature.
HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit temperature-dependent elastically anisotropic deformation.
HfNbTaTiZr will retain high yield strength at elevated temperatures.
HfNbTaTiZr will show substantial resistance to thermal softening at elevated temperatures.
HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit a unique elevated-temperature deformation behavior.
The hypothesis may remain applicable up to the alloy's melting point or beyond.
Changing strain rate will access different deformation mechanisms.
The proposed mechanism applies to either polycrystalline or single-crystal HfNbTaTiZr.

contradictions.description: The initial state permits a single crystal, but grain boundaries and grain-boundary sliding are presented as general mediators and mechanisms; an ideal single crystal lacks grain boundaries.
The scope extends to or beyond melting, whereas dislocation slip, grain-boundary sliding, elastic anisotropy, yield strength, and solid-state stress–strain behavior require a solid alloy.
